chapter_meta_description: Han Li faces Xiao Chan, the ‘Profound Bone Saint,’ a living corpse from an era before the founding of Extreme Yin Island. Cold negotiations and mutual suspicion replace all-out war.
og_title: A Mortal’s Journey – The Profound Bone Saint Is Unmasked
og_description: Han Li faces the thousand-year old ghost Xiao Chan. No heroism, no camaraderie—just two survivors probing each other for weaknesses.
twitter_title: RMJI Ch. 435: The Ghost Saint Shows his True Form
twitter_description: Han Li and Xiao Chan exchange subtle threats, buried secrets, and forced politeness in a battle of information warfare.

lore_anchors.definition: A legendary plant material used to refine lightning-attributed magical treasures. It can be “pure” (Gold Lightning Bamboo) or corrupted by demonic Qi, producing black lightning that is even more aggressive.

A special undead-like state where a cultivator disperses their Nascent Soul to become a pure spirit entity, bypassing physical lifespan limits at the cost of severe restrictions like vulnerability to sunlight.
The title of Xiao Chan, a legendary cultivator who claims to be the master of Extreme Yin Island’s founder. He is over a thousand years old and exists as a Profound Soul Body.
A subspecies of Divine Thunder Bamboo that produces golden lightning known as “Righteous Demon-Suppressing Lightning.” Extremely rare and nearly extinct in the Chaos Star Sea.
A second body or clone cultivated using a Demon Core, a dark-aligned cultivation outcome. Possession of one marks a cultivator as potentially connected to demonic-path practices.

cultural_notes_faq.a: He is the Profound Bone Saint, a ghost-like entity who claims to be the master of the founder of Extreme Yin Island. He is over a thousand years old and exists in a Profound Soul Body, having sacrificed his physical form for vengeance.

cultural_notes_faq.q: Why does Han Li’s bamboo lose to the arrow?
cultural_notes_faq.a: The seven Bamboo Cloudswarm Swords are freshly cultivated and rely purely on their innate lightning. Xiao Chan’s arrow has been corrupted by black demonic Qi and tempered for far longer, making it overpowered even against pure lightning.

cultural_notes_faq.q: What is the “Profound Soul Body” Xiao Chan mentions?
cultural_notes_faq.a: A technique that allows a cultivator to abandon their physical body and become a spirit entity, bypassing ordinary lifespan limits but forfeiting reincarnation and suffering critical weaknesses (like vulnerability to sunlight).

cultural_notes_faq.q: Why do Han Li and Xiao Chan stop fighting?
cultural_notes_faq.a: Both realize a full confrontation would cost too much. Han Li has his beetles, Xiao Chan has centuries of demonic experience and a superior lightning treasure. They reach a cold standoff rather than a resolution.

cultural_notes_faq.q: Is Han Li’s story about the jade slip true?
cultural_notes_faq.a: Probably, but the real question isn’t truth—it’s whether Xiao Chan will accept it. The chapter ends on a mutual information standoff, not a confession.
